cohort: Patients presenting with postpartum hemorrhage following delivery at R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, West Bengal, India (n=304, representing 1.4% of 22,182 deliveries).
finding: Atonic PPH was the most common type of PPH (50.6% overall) and was responsible for most maternal deaths (75%), and uterine tamponade was the most successful treatment for PPH following vaginal delivery (86.66%).
mod_finding: In instrumental deliveries, traumatic PPH was more prevalent (50%), while in Cesarean sections, atonic PPH was more prevalent (80.64%).
